The HCF of two numbers is one-twentieth of their LCM. If one of the numbers is 96 and the difference of the LCM and the HCF is 456, then what is the other number?
questions.solution_en:
Let other number = x

Let LCM = y

HCF = y/20

=> LCM - HCF = 456

y - y/20 = 456

y = 480

LCM = 480

HCF = 480/20 = 24

Product of two numbers = LCM * HCF

96 * x = 480 * 24

x = 120

questions.q_en: Rishabh bought few notebooks for ₹900 from a bookstore. He negotiated the price and the shopkeeper reduced it by ₹5 per notebook. Due to this Rishabh could buy two more notebooks than what he had bought earlier. How many notebooks did he originally buy?
questions.solution_en:
Let cost price of a notebook = ₹P

Number of notebooks = N

P * N = 900

After negotiation:

Cost price of a notebook = ₹(P - 5)

Number of notebooks = N + 2

(P - 5)(N + 2) = 900

(900/N - 5)(N + 2) = 900

(180 - N)(N + 2) = 180N

N2 + 2N - 360 = 0

N2 + 20N - 18N - 360 = 0

(N - 18) (N + 20) = 0

N = 18

Number of notebooks = 18

questions.q_en: A can complete 25% of a work in 15 days. He works for 15 days and then B alone finishes the remaining work in 30 days. In how many days will A and B working together finish 50% of the same work?
questions.solution_en:
Time in which A alone can complete the whole work = 15 * 100/25 = 60 days

15 days' work done by A alone = 15/60 = 1/4

Remaining work = 1 - 1/4 = 3/4

Now, time in which B alone can complete the whole work = 30 * 4/3 = 40 days

Therefore, time taken by A and B together to finish 50% of the work

= 50/100 * 1/(1/60 + 1/40)

= 12 days

questions.q_en: Prakash's 5 day's work is equal to Suresh's 3 day's work and ratio of efficiency of Suresh to Krishna is 4: 3. Suresh and Krishna started working together and worked for 4 days. After that Krishna left the work and Prakash joined Suresh and they together worked for next 5 days. Now Suresh left the work and Prakash alone finished the remaining work in 5 more day. Find that in how many days Suresh can finish the work alone?
questions.solution_en:
Prakash's 5 day's work is equal to Suresh's 3 day's work. So ratio of their efficiency = 1/5 ∶1/3 = 3 : 5

Ratio of efficiency of Suresh to Krishna = 4 : 3

The ratio of efficiency of Prakash, Suresh and Krishna = 12 : 20 : 15

Let 1 day of work of Prakash, Suresh and Krishan is 12x, 20x and 15x respectively.

Total work = (20x + 15x) * 4 + (12x + 20x) * 5 + 12x * 5 = 360x

Time taken by Suresh alone to finish the work = 360x/20x = 18 days

questions.q_en: Two stations R and S are 400 km apart from each other. A train leaves from R to S and simultaneously another train leaves from S to R. Both trains meet after 10 hours. If the speed of the first train is 4 km/h more than the second train, then what is the speed of the slower train?
questions.solution_en:
Let the speed of slower and faster train is 's' km/h and 's + 4' km/h.

Relative speed of both the trains when travelling towards each other = s + (s + 4) = (2s + 4) km/h

Distance between both the trains = 400 km

(2s + 4) * 10 = 400

2s + 4 = 40

s = 18

Speed of slower train = s = 18 km/h

questions.q_en: A and B together can do a piece of work in 14 days, B and C together can do the same piece of work in 20 days and C and A together can do the same piece of work in 15 days. They all work together for 10 days after which A and B leave the work. How many days C will take to finish the remaining work?
questions.solution_en:
Let total work = LCM of 14, 20, and 15 = 420 units

Efficiency of A and B = 420/14 = 30 units per day

Efficiency of B and C = 420/20 = 21 units per day

Efficiency of C and A = 420/15 = 28 units per day

2 * (A + B + C) = 79

A + B + C = 79/2

Efficiency of C = (79/2) - 30 = 19/2 units per day

Work done by A, B, and C in 10 days = 79 * 10/2 = 395

Remaining work = 420 - 395 = 25 units

Required number of days = 25 * 2/19 = 50/19 = 2(12/19) days.

Total amount of tin = 30 + 25 = 55 kg
